title: Integral Mean Value Theorem
q_prose: Given four functions psi one, psi two, f, and g on non-negative real numbers, decide which of the four statements is true.
q_narration: We have four functions on non negative real numbers, and we must decide which statement is true; let us solve step by step.

steps.label: Step 1 — Link the functions
steps.narration: Differentiate psi two. Its derivative is exactly two times psi one minus one, so this is the key link.

steps.label: Step 2 — Apply mean value theorem
steps.narration: Since psi two at zero is zero, the mean value theorem on the interval from zero to any positive input gives a beta strictly between zero and that input. Substituting the derivative relation gives exactly option C.

steps.label: Step 3 — Reject option A
steps.narration: For option A, after using evenness and the substitution t equals u square in the second integral, the sum simplifies to one minus e power minus input square. At root log three, the value is two by three, not one by three.

steps.label: Step 4 — Reject option B
steps.narration: For option B, the required alpha would be less than one for every positive input. So it cannot lie between one and the input.

steps.label: Step 5 — Reject option D
steps.narration: For option D, the derivative of f becomes negative after one. Hence f decreases on part of the interval from zero to three by two, so it is not increasing there.

answer_narration: Therefore only option C is true. Keep practicing with Acharya for more clear step by step solutions.
options: For every $x>1$, there exists an $\alpha \in(1, x)$ such that $\psi_{1}(x)=1+\alpha x$
For every $x>0$, there exists a $\beta \in(0, x)$ such that $\psi_{2}(x)=2 x\left(\psi_{1}(\beta)-1\right)$
$f$ is an increasing function on the interval $\left[0, \frac{3}{2}\right]$
